overview.short: Indori fort also known as Induri Fort (Marathi: इन्दुरी किल्ला)is one of the many Land forts of Maharashtra state in India.
overview.description: Indori fort also known as Induri Fort (Marathi: इन्दुरी किल्ला)is one of the many Land forts of Maharashtra state in India. Situated close to the hill station Lonavala and 35 km (22 mi) north of Pune, Indori fort rises to an elevation of 1,033 m (3,389 ft) above sea level. The fort is located on the banks of Indrayani River. The fort was under the Maratha Empire for the majority of the time.

topPlaces.name: Ghorawadi Caves
topPlaces.description: Ancient 3rd-century Buddhist rock-cut caves and rock-carved Shiva sanctum nestled on a high hill overlooking the old Mumbai-Pune highway.

image.alt: Ghorawadi Caves — Indori Fort, Maharashtra scenic view

topPlaces.name: Prati Shirdi Temple, Shirgaon
topPlaces.description: Renowned temple complex modeled as an authentic replica of the sacred shrine in Shirdi, surrounded by ornate sanctums and peaceful gardens.

image.alt: Traditional temple shikhara and sanctum architecture in Maharashtra

topPlaces.name: Talegaon Dabhade Heritage Lake
topPlaces.description: Historic 18th-century stone reservoir built by the noble Dabhade family (Senapati of the Maratha Empire), fringed by ancient trees and heritage temples.

image.alt: Tranquil freshwater reservoir lake surrounded by lush green Maval hills in Talegaon

topPlaces.name: Bhandara Dongar
topPlaces.description: Sacred hill overlooking the Indrayani river valley where saint-poet Sant Tukaram meditated, offering breathtaking panoramic vistas of the Sahyadri ranges.

image.alt: Aerial panoramic vista of lush green hills and valleys around Bhandara Dongar

topPlaces.name: Dehu Gatha Mandir
topPlaces.description: Venerated pilgrimage complex constructed on the holy banks of the Indrayani River, enshrining the sacred abhangas carved in stone.

image.alt: Dehu Gatha Mandir — Indori Fort, Maharashtra scenic view

topPlaces.name: Lohagad Fort
topPlaces.description: Majestic Maratha hill fortress towering 1,033 meters above sea level, famed for its formidable stone bastions and the iconic Vinchukata spur.

image.alt: Monumental stone bastions and mountain ramparts of Lohagad Fort near Indori

topPlaces.name: Karla Caves
topPlaces.description: Spectacular 2nd-century BCE Buddhist rock-cut chaitya hall featuring colossal sculpted stone pillars and the original teak wood ribbed roof.

image.alt: Karla Caves — Indori Fort, Maharashtra scenic view

topPlaces.name: Bhaja Caves
topPlaces.description: Cluster of 22 ancient Buddhist rock-cut caves renowned for exquisite relief carvings, wooden architecture replicas, and monolithic stone stupas.

image.alt: Bhaja Caves — Indori Fort, Maharashtra scenic view

items.note: Induri is a village and gram panchayat in India, situated in Mawal taluka of Pune district in the state of Maharashtra. It encompasses an area of 1,531.07 ha (3,783 acres).
Nanoli Tarf Chakan is a village and gram panchayat in India, situated in Mawal taluka of Pune district in the state of Maharashtra. It encompasses an area of 496 ha (1,226 acres).
Talegaon is a town on the outskirts of the city of Pune, India.
Ambi is a village and gram panchayat in India, situated in Mawal taluka of Pune district in the state of Maharashtra. It encompasses an area of 819 ha (2,024 acres).

The Ghorawadi caves, also known as Ghoradeshwar caves or Shelarwadi caves, are around 25 km (16 mi) northwest of Pune, India, were originally Buddhist caves, and now contain carvings and statues of Buddhist and Hindu deities. They are close to the NH4 highway connecting Pune and Mumbai.
Shirgaon is a village and gram panchayat in Mawal taluka of Pune district in the state of Maharashtra, India. It encompasses an area of 389.66 ha (963 acres).
Somatane is an Indian village and gram panchayat located in Mawal taluka of Pune district, Maharashtra. It encompasses an area of 434.04 ha (1,073 acres).

items.activity: B K Birla Centre For Education
items.note: B K Birla Centre For Education is a Boys' residential school located near Pune, India. Affiliated to the Central Board of Secondary Education syllabus, it caters for 600 students from class IV to XII. The school's first principal was G. C. Rao, who was further succeeded by S. K. Bhardwaj and then Subhash Kumar.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Indori Fort?
faq.a: The best time to visit Indori Fort is Oct – Mar. Summers are 26–40°C and winters are 12–28°C.

faq.q: How do I reach Indori Fort?
faq.a: The nearest airport is Indori Fort / nearest airport (30 km) and the nearest railway station is Pune Junction (29 km). Roads are generally good; check seasonal/monsoon conditions before high-altitude or remote stretches.

faq.q: How many days are enough for Indori Fort?
faq.a: 3 days are usually enough to cover the top attractions of Indori Fort at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: How much does a hotel cost in Indori Fort?
faq.a: Stays in Indori Fort start from ₹900 per night, with options across 4 price categories.

faq.q: What are the top places to visit in Indori Fort?
faq.a: The top attractions are Induri, Nanoli Tarf Chakan, Talegaon Dabhade, Ambi, Mawal, Ghorawadi Caves.
